solomon.title: Solomon’s Temple: From courtyard to covenant

chapters.title: The courtyard
chapters.text: Before the temple Jesus knew, there was Solomon's. Let's begin in its courtyard, with the sanctuary ahead.

chapters.title: The bronze pillars
chapters.text: Two bronze pillars frame the entrance. First Kings names them Jachin and Boaz.

chapters.title: Worked bronze
chapters.text: Lily-shaped capitals, latticework and pomegranates bring the bronze to life. Their exact appearance remains an artist's interpretation.

chapters.title: The Holy Place
chapters.text: Inside, gold covers the timber. Ten lampstands stand before the inner room, five on each side.

chapters.title: Light and carved timber
chapters.text: The lamps draw our eyes along walls carved with palms, flowers and cherubim.

chapters.title: The Most Holy Place
chapters.text: Beyond the doors, two great cherubim spread their wings above the Ark in the Most Holy Place.

chapters.title: The Ark of the Covenant
chapters.text: Here, the covenant has a physical reminder: the Ark holding the stone tablets Moses placed inside.

captions.text:
Before the temple Jesus knew, there was
Solomon's.

Let's begin in its courtyard, with the
sanctuary ahead.
Two bronze pillars frame the entrance.
First Kings names them Jachin and Boaz.

Lily-shaped capitals, latticework and
pomegranates bring the bronze to life.

Their exact appearance remains an artist's
interpretation.
Inside, gold covers the timber.
Ten lampstands stand before the inner room,
five on each side.
The lamps draw our eyes along walls carved
with palms, flowers and cherubim.
Beyond the doors, two great cherubim
spread their wings above the Ark
in the Most Holy Place.
Here, the covenant has a physical reminder:
the Ark holding the stone tablets
Moses placed inside.

herod.title: Herod’s Temple: The temple Jesus knew

chapters.title: The Royal Stoa
chapters.text: By Jesus' time, Herod had transformed Jerusalem's temple. Along the southern edge stood the Royal Stoa, a great colonnaded hall.

chapters.title: The Holy Place
chapters.text: Our view follows ancient descriptions, with some details interpreted. Within the sanctuary, a lampstand, bread table and incense altar furnished the Holy Place.

chapters.title: The seven lamps
chapters.text: Seven lamps burn on a single golden stand. Beyond the sanctuary lay the courts where Jesus walked and taught.

ezekiel.title: Ezekiel’s Temple: From exile to life

chapters.title: The wider precinct
chapters.text: Jerusalem has fallen. Far from home, the prophet Ezekiel sees a temple in a vision.

chapters.title: The outer gateway
chapters.text: A guide with a measuring reed leads him through its gates, measuring as they go.

chapters.title: Inside the gateway
chapters.text: We're picturing that account here. Its measurements guide us; some details are an artist's interpretation.
chapters.passage: An artistic reconstruction guided by Ezekiel 40–48

chapters.title: The altar in its court
chapters.text: In the inner court stands an altar, with steps facing east, before the sanctuary.

chapters.title: The sanctuary entrance
chapters.text: The vision carries a promise for Israel: God will dwell among his people.

chapters.title: The timber-lined hall
chapters.text: Inside, carved timber surrounds a wooden altar, described as the table before the Lord.

chapters.title: Palms and two faces
chapters.text: Palms alternate with cherubim, each bearing two faces: a human and a young lion.

chapters.title: Water from the threshold
chapters.text: Then water emerges beneath the threshold. In Ezekiel's vision, it becomes a river that brings life.

captions.text: Jerusalem has fallen.

sees a temple in a vision.
A guide with a measuring reed

leads him through its gates,
measuring as they go.

Its measurements guide us;
some details are an artist's interpretation.
In the inner court stands an altar,

with steps facing east,
before the sanctuary.
The vision carries a promise for Israel:
God will dwell among his people.

Inside, carved timber surrounds
a wooden altar,
described as the table before the Lord.
Palms alternate with cherubim,

each bearing two faces:
a human and a young lion.
Then water emerges beneath the threshold.
In Ezekiel's vision, it becomes a river
that brings life.
